memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So Jacob said to his household and to all who were with him, 'Get rid of the foreign gods you have with you, and purify yourselves and change your clothes. Then come, let us go up to Bethel, where I will build an altar to God, who answered me in the day of my distress and who has been with me wherever I have gone.' So they gave Jacob all the foreign gods they had and the rings in their ears, and Jacob buried them under the oak at Shechem." - Gen 35:2-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before the family can go up to meet God at Bethel, Jacob calls for a spiritual housecleaning: "Get rid of the foreign gods you have with you, and purify yourselves." All this time, idols had been quietly hiding in the household — the very ones Rachel had carried off (Gen 31:19). Now they are gathered up and buried under the oak at Shechem. The family cannot go forward to worship the living God while still clinging to false ones.

This is a powerful picture of what it means to return to God. Coming back to Him involves letting go of the idols we have been holding on to. We cannot draw near to God with one hand while gripping our substitutes for Him with the other.

What are the "foreign gods" in your life — the things that quietly compete for the devotion that belongs to God alone? It may be money, comfort, approval, a habit, a relationship, an ambition. Whatever it is, returning to God means burying it, laying it down decisively so it no longer rules the heart.

Notice that they did not merely hide the idols; they gave them up and buried them. Real repentance is decisive. As you go up to your Bethel, take an honest look at what you are carrying, and let God help you bury it. Whole-hearted worship requires a heart cleared of rivals.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What "foreign gods" am I still quietly holding on to?
2. Is there an idol I need to decisively bury, not just hide?
3. What would it mean to purify my heart before God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, show me the idols I have been carrying, and give me grace to bury them decisively. Cleanse my heart of every rival, so I may worship You wholeheartedly. Amen.
